subject: Proposal: staged uplift with commit forgiveness and co-term alignment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Miller <sara@veridianhealth.com>, procurement@veridianhealth.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: staged uplift with commit forgiveness and co-term alignment

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a compact proposal that aims to let Veridian scale across Q4 while limiting near-term budget impact. Key ideas below: 

- Staged uplift: two tranches over 12 months (50% immediate, 50% at 6 months) to smooth invoice impact.
- Co-term alignment: we’ll align the uplift to your existing renewal date so you only manage one renewal in 12 months.
- Forgiveness cushion: up to 15% of the bumped capacity can be marked as "forgivable" if actual usage stays below projected run-rate at month 6 (applies only to committed GPU-hours).
- Early top-up discount: 8% off the incremental uplift if Veridian approves and pays the first tranche within 14 days.

I’ve attached a short one-page offer (Veridian_Sprint-Offer-v3.pdf) and a MOP summary with the forgiveness mechanics (MOP-voucher-summary.xlsx).

Requested next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether procurement needs a single PO that covers both tranches or two separate POs?
2) Are there any internal approvals we should schedule for a fast-track (14 day) sign?

If it helps I’m happy to jump on a quick 20-min call with your procurement team to walk through the forgiveness language.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Veridian_Sprint-Offer-v3.pdf (proposal, 3 pages); MOP-voucher-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 tab)

From: Sara Miller <sara@veridianhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged uplift with commit forgiveness and co-term alignment

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear options. A few quick questions from my side and procurement: 

- Can you explain why the forgiveness cushion is capped at 15%? Our forecasts are conservative but have spikes — curious if that floor can be 20%.
- For the early top-up discount: does that apply to both tranches or only the incremental capacity in tranche 1?
- Procurement asked whether Redwoods’ invoice will show a single aggregated line item or three lines (commit, forgiveness reserve, voucher). They prefer a single line if possible.

Also looping procurement so they have the docs.

On Thu we have a standing vendor sync at 3pm PT — is that a good time to take this?

Best,

Sara — thanks for the questions. Quick clarifications and an updated option set below. Ben and Naomi: feel free to edit wording for legal/procurement clarity.

1) Forgiveness cap rationale: we chose 15% to balance predictability for pricing and operational buffer for you. That said, we can move to 20% for a 1.5% reduction in the early-top-up discount (so early-top-up becomes 6.5% instead of 8%).

2) Early top-up discount application: the discount applies only to the incremental capacity purchased in tranche 1 (i.e., the first 50% uplift). If you want it applied to both tranches we can offer 4.5% off tranche 2 (reflects additional cash-flow risk).

3) Invoice presentation: we can present a single invoice line that reads: "Committed Inference Capacity (monthly amortized) — includes forgiveable reserve" with an attached MOP workbook that breaks down the internal accounting lines for your finance team. Procurement will have the visibility but your AP sees one line.

4) Additional optionality: if Veridian signs within 14 days we will include a clause to accelerate tranche 2 timing by up to 60 days at no additional fee (helps if you plan immediate ramp).

Suggested next steps:
- If procurement prefers single PO, we’ll draft a one-PO amendment and share for legal redlines.
- If Veridian wants 20% forgiveness, confirm and we’ll reflect the 1.5% change to early-top-up discount on the term sheet.

Ben: I uploaded a redlined offer (see Veridian_Sprint-Offer-v3.pdf) and a revised MOP (MOP-voucher-summary.xlsx) to the deal record. I’ll be on the vendor sync Thu 3pm PT.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

priyom_das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
